newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve flattens over past week - Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve flattens over past week - Delphis.

text.p: The municipal yield curve flattened five to 10 basis points for most investment-grade sectors in the week ended Thursday, Delphis Hanover Corp. said Friday.
The flattening came as yields on short-term bonds held steady while long-term and intermediate yields fell during the week.
The Baa yield curve between one-year and thirty-year bonds flattened 10 basis points to 175 basis points, reversing the prior week's 10 basis point steepening.
The spread between one-year and 30-year bonds in the triple-A category steepened five basis points to 180, but every other investment-grade category saw flattening.
Average yields on one-year, Aaa-rated municipal bonds fell five basis points to 3.80 percent, while Baa-rated one-year bonds were unchanged at 4.60 percent.

The intermediate sector lost five basis points across the credit spectrum, after shedding 10 basis points in each of the previous two weeks. Yields on Aaa-rated 10-year bonds dropped five to 4.90 percent and Baa-rated ten-years fell five to 5.75 percent.
Long-term municipals continued to outperform the Treasury market over the week, as low new issue supply bolstered prices.

The yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond fell six basis points to 6.87 percent. Thirty-year municipal yields, meanwhile, were unchanged at 5.60 percent, after falling 20 basis points over the previous three weeks.
Yields were down 10 basis points on 30-year, Baa-rated bonds, falling to 6.35 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis yielded 81.5 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, compared to 80.8 percent the week before.

The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years widened five basis points to 80 basis points, reversing the prior week's narrowing. The 30-year spread narrowed 10 to 75 basis points, after widening five the prior week.
